title: Call for new provincial and federal municipal funding framework
subtitle: Also: 2024 budget kickoff, development charge changes, transit fares, police budget process and a stalled letter request.
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee opened the 2024 budget season by recommending that the Region formally ask Ontario to commit to a new municipal fiscal funding framework. It also asked the province and Ottawa to review the current framework with municipalities. Following an amendment, the request will go to other Ontario municipalities, local MPs and MPPs, AMO and FCM. It will also go to the Prime Minister, the Premier and the finance and municipal affairs ministers, asking for a committee or task force. The committee recommended this {{vote:m2}}.

The motion argues that property taxes are being used to pay for services that should be funded by senior governments, and that this gets harder as the region grows toward 1 million people. Councils may adopt or change these recommendations later.

Staff then presented a draft 2024 plan and budget. It covered economic conditions, the effects of provincial development charge changes, and the review schedule. The preliminary budget will be tabled on October 18, with public input meetings and a December 13 approval day. This was an information session, not a budget decision.
A request to send a letter to the Police Services Board about pre-budget presentations did not advance, because a motion to waive notice was defeated {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region ask Ontario to commit to a new municipal fiscal funding framework, and ask the province and Government of Canada to review the current one openly with municipalities.

The committee amended the motion so it is sent to all Ontario municipalities, local MPs and MPPs, AMO and FCM, and to federal and provincial leaders and ministers requesting a committee or task force.

decisions.item: Waiving notice for fiscal framework motion
decisions.detail: The committee waived the notice requirement so the municipal fiscal framework motion could be considered at this meeting.

decisions.item: Notice waiver for Police Services Board letter
decisions.detail: A motion to waive notice, to allow a request for a letter asking the Police Services Board to respond to Council's earlier pre-budget request, was defeated, so that request did not proceed.

debate: Councillors argued that the Region is covering costs that belong to senior governments. They said this normalizes the arrangement for residents and for the province, and that advocacy should become more assertive.

One councillor called the original wording weak, saying the province could simply not respond. This led to the amendment sending the motion to the Premier and ministers and asking for a committee or task force. Others suggested adding the Prime Minister, the municipal affairs minister and other municipalities, and asked whether one joint or separate bodies were meant.

Several councillors said residents should direct their frustration at MPs and MPPs rather than local councils. Others said the effort is stronger if many municipalities pass similar motions, so that governments cannot play them off against each other.

On the budget, councillors asked why falling inflation does not mean lower prices. Staff said lower inflation applies on top of earlier increases, so cumulative prices stay higher. Councillors also raised the proposed cash transit fare change, saying some riders cannot prepay or use cards. Staff said the aim is to move people off cash and that fare changes will return for decision.

Councillors disagreed over police budget process. One wanted a pre-budget presentation and a letter to the Police Services Board. Others said the board is independent and Council can only approve the bottom line, and that a report on the history and rules was already promised. Another said Council had in effect already received a response.
